deficiencies.description: The text states that 'invasion and malignancy' are diagnostically important and then states 'it's defined as the ability to invade the surrounding tissue', leaving it unclear whether 'it' refers to invasion or malignancy. The rewrite resolves this ambiguity by explicitly attributing the definition to malignancy.
deficiencies.sourcePassage: So invasion and malignancy are really, really important diagnostically. So it's defined as the ability to invade the surrounding tissue.
deficiencies.rewritePassage: Invasion and malignancy are very important diagnostically, and malignancy is defined as the ability to invade the surrounding tissue.
deficiencies.caseForHarm: A student reading the rewrite is taught definitively that the lecturer was defining malignancy rather than invasion, when the lecturer's singular pronoun after a compound subject was ambiguous.
deficiencies.caseAgainstHarm: In pathology, malignancy is standardly defined by the capacity of a tumour to invade surrounding tissue, whereas defining invasion as the ability to invade would be circular, so the rewrite simply selects the only medically coherent antecedent.

considerations.sourcePassage: So this is probably an obligatory step in getting to having a malignant metastasizing tumor.
considerations.reason: The rewrite renders 'this' as 'Invasion', which is justified by the surrounding context discussing how tumours invade before they can metastasise, so the pointing word is supported by the text.
The change to 'muscularis mucosae' reflects the term correction provided in the prompt.

considerations.reason: The dropped rhetorical question about secondary metastases was an abandoned aside that the lecturer immediately set aside to resume describing the histology under the microscope.
